A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nonlinear preconditioning can be very efficient for the solution of steady and unsteady problems, if the preconditioner is properly chosen.
we show how to use nonlinear schemes in Newton–Kyrlov methods in an efficient manner.
we have shown the equivalence of nonlinear schemes like the dual time‐stepping and the Newton method.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the convergence behavior of the nonlinear preconditioner is determined by the linearization of the preconditioner, and that the nonlinear preconditioner itself does not have to be linearly convergent to be a good preconditioner.
the nonlinear preconditioner can be interpreted as a linear operator, and this linear operator has a certain structure that can be exploited in the analysis of the convergence properties.
the nonlinear schemes can be used as preconditioners, but they do not necessarily improve the convergence rate of the Newton method.
